If it is a provider node, please contact the service provider to complete the technical upgrade. If the service provider refuses to cooperate, it is recommended to switch to a provider that pays more attention to user security.

GUTS carries the phone’s traffic through a Google Apps Script door to an exit node, and only needs Google to be reachable. It is a TCP tunnel: UDP, QUIC, calls and games stay off, and the door’s daily Apps Script quota is shared by everything that uses it.

Certificate mode needs no exit node and no /g URL. Omni ends HTTPS on this phone with your own local CA, sends ordinary web requests to your Apps Script, and Apps Script fetches the site. Google and YouTube HTTPS bypass Apps Script through the selected Google edge, because YouTube treats Apps Script fetches as automated traffic. Install the certificate below once. This carries HTTP/HTTPS for browsers and apps that trust a user-installed CA; it is not raw TCP, UDP, calls or games.
On: the door fetches websites itself and HTTPS ends at your local certificate. Off: the old raw-TCP exit-node mode.

GUTS works as the profile itself, or as the last step of a proxy chain — the tunnel the chain is dialled through. It cannot sit in the middle of a chain, inside a policy group, or beside another native core.
